description:
Hey there! 

I am creating a web based tool that will help users during their Earth-science investigation.

Relevant (but not limited to) skills for this solution are:

Data analysis - for statistical analysis testing on data + plotting

UI design - for interactive frontend

Prompt engineering - for better documentation and brainstorming using AI

Familiarity with scientific trend analysis
summary:
Detectro+  is an investigation-driven climate trend analyzer webapp . It helps user to investigate environmental change using NASA Earth data. It addresses the challenge by connecting questions to measurable indicators, visualizing change and explaining statistical evidence.
It is built for users from scientific-background and college level students. 
App uses research-inspired concept recognition, named entity recognition and semantic query expansion, supported by Gemini and a curated variable catalog. Its STAT engine applies Seasonal Mann–Kendall, Sen’s slope and seasonal regression to examine trend direction, magnitude and uncertainty.

Provided static demonstration explores off-season rainfall near Jamshoro around the 2022 floods using NASA POWER/MERRA-2 precipitation, temperature and humidity data from 2001–2024. Interactive charts, spatial grids, standardized comparisons, explanatory tooltips and a written report help students interpret the evidence.

The current demo uses precomputed real data for one investigation and supports informed exploration without claiming that observed changes establish causation.
details:
Detectro+ is a web-based climate trend analyzer that helps user to investigate environmental change using NASA Earth data. It addresses a common difficulty in trend analysis: knowing which indicators to examine, how much they changed and whether the evidence supports a sustained trend.

How it works:

User enter investigation and provide with region , geographic area and time period. The backend maps the question to supported scientific variables, prepares monthly regional data and runs statistical analysis. Interactive plots, spatial grids and an explanatory report helps user interpret the results and find valuable trends.

Provided static prototype doesnot include filters and query entry rather showcase provided investigation analysis flow.

Selecting Relevant Scientific Indicators:

Inspired by Query Understanding Framework for Earth Data Discovery, the investigation/query is processed using 3 modular framework: concept recognition, named entity recognition and semantic query expansion for fetching effective indicators to analyze trend.

Final indicators are fetched by Gemini based on the investigation’s scientific meaning , synonyms and the curated catalog’s variable names taken from NASA researches and assimilation model.

For example, “rainfall” maps to precipitation (PRECTOTCORR), whose MERRA-2-derived values are obtained through NASA POWER.

Statistical Methods Used for analysis:

  • Monthly anomalies: reveal departures from usual seasonal conditions.
  • Seasonal Mann–Kendall: examines sustained increases or decreases while accounting for seasonality.
  • Sen’s slope: estimates the rate of change.
  • Seasonal regression with robust uncertainty: provides a complementary trend estimate and confidence interval.
  • Standardized slopes: compare changes across variables with different units.

Dependence checks flag limitations that can affect statistical significance.

NASA Data & Demonstration:

The proposed investigation demo examines rainfall near Jamshoro district around the 2022 floods using NASA POWER/MERRA-2 data from 2001–2024. Precipitation is the primary indicator, with temperature and humidity preselected as context. Results are precomputed, while charts and reports remain interactive.

Key Benefits & Intended Impact:

  • Helps students connect questions to measurable evidence.
  • Preserves monthly spikes while examining long-term patterns.
  • Explains scientific terms and evidences through tooltips and readable reports.
  • Encourages interpretation of uncertainty and separation of association from causation.

Tools & Technologies:

The proposed prototype uses Next.js, React, TypeScript, CSS and Recharts for its interface and interactive visualizations. It displays bundled NASA POWER data and precomputed statistical results.

Creative Elements:

Detectro+ combines investigation understanding, scientific indicator selection and statistical explanation within one investigation workflow, helping students become active interpreters of Earth data.

Future implementation: Integrate a ReSearch-based dataset retrieval layer to map Earth-science variables/indicators with effective NASA datasets.
projectRefs: Query Understanding Framework for Earth Data Discovery
